topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the course structure, personal background, and core learning objectives on cancer etiology.

topics.label: Origins of Cancer: Intrinsic Mutations versus Environmental Exposures
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational concepts of cancer etiology, evaluating the relative contributions of endogenous mutations, random chance, and environmental exposures.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how viral and bacterial infections contribute to malignant transformation, illustrated in detail by the mechanism of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how specific environmental, dietary, and chemical mutagens undergo metabolic activation and induce DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain non-mutagenic mechanisms of cancer development, focusing on tumor promoters, chronic inflammation, and developmental windows of tissue susceptibility.

topics.label: Methods for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to determine carcinogenicity and assess cancer risk.
